_meta.note: Human-vetted question bank. Each module's questions are grounded in that module's lesson text. assess.ts serves a randomised subset with shuffled options; grading is deterministic against the 'correct' index here.

intro.q: What is "AI Fluency" as defined in this course?
options: The ability to program AI systems and train models
The ability to work with AI systems effectively, efficiently, ethically, and safely
A certification required before you may use Claude at work
The academic study of how AI models are built
intro.explanation: AI Fluency is defined as working with AI effectively, efficiently, ethically and safely — not about becoming a programmer or researcher.

intro.q: Who developed the AI Fluency framework?
options: Professors Joseph Feller and Rick Dakan, in partnership with Anthropic
intro.explanation: It was developed by Prof. Joseph Feller (University College Cork) and Prof. Rick Dakan (Ringling College), in partnership with Anthropic.

intro.q: According to the AI Fluency Index research, roughly what share of the most effective AI conversations involve iteration and refinement?
intro.explanation: Research showed 85.7% of the most effective conversations involve iteration — the best outcomes come from skilled collaboration, not the first answer.

intro.q: AI Fluency requires you to become which of the following?
options: Neither — it is about practical competencies for collaborating with AI as a professional tool
intro.explanation: The module stresses it is not about becoming a programmer or researcher, but developing practical collaboration competencies.

intro.q: Why is AI fluency framed as a particular opportunity for South African SMEs?
options: AI tools are free in South Africa
It lets smaller firms augment their capabilities and compete with larger organisations without matching headcount
POPIA legally requires businesses to use AI
Local AI models outperform global ones
intro.explanation: SMEs can leapfrog productivity barriers and compete with larger organisations by using AI to augment capability rather than matching headcount.

4d-overview.q: What are the four competencies of the 4D Framework?
4d-overview.explanation: The four Ds are Delegation, Description, Discernment, and Diligence.

4d-overview.q: Which competency is the critical evaluation of AI output — telling accurate from plausible-but-wrong?
4d-overview.explanation: Discernment is the critical evaluation of output, including spotting gaps, errors, and hallucinations.

4d-overview.q: How does the framework describe the relationship between the four competencies?
options: Sequential steps to be followed in strict order
An interconnected system in which each competency reinforces the others
Ranked from most to least important
4d-overview.explanation: They are not sequential steps — they are an interconnected, holistic system.

4d-overview.q: Which competency covers data privacy, transparency about AI involvement, and accuracy verification?
4d-overview.explanation: Diligence covers the ethical, legal, and professional responsibility dimensions of AI use.

4d-overview.q: Description involves specifying which three things?
4d-overview.explanation: Description covers what you want (product), how to approach it (process), and how the AI should behave (performance).

delegation.q: What are the three modes of AI interaction described in this module?
delegation.explanation: The three modes are Automation, Augmentation, and Agency.

delegation.q: Collaborative work where human and AI contribute complementary strengths is called:
delegation.explanation: Augmentation is collaborative work with complementary strengths — where most knowledge work with AI falls.

delegation.q: Which task is the BEST candidate for AI according to the decision matrix?
options: Summarising meeting notes, where errors are low-risk and easy to verify
delegation.explanation: Low-risk tasks with straightforward verification are excellent AI candidates; high-stakes tasks need human leadership.

delegation.q: "AI operates with significant autonomy within guardrails you establish" describes which mode?
delegation.explanation: Agency is the mode with the most AI autonomy, requiring the highest level of trust and oversight.

delegation.q: Effective delegation requires which two things?
delegation.explanation: You need domain expertise (you understand the work) and platform awareness (you understand what AI can and cannot do).

description.q: Product description (format, audience, length, domain constraints) primarily defines:
options: The steps the AI should follow
description.explanation: Product description specifies the output itself.

description.q: "First identify the key issues, then evaluate each, then rank by priority, then draft recommendations" is an example of:
description.explanation: Process description tells the AI how to work through the task — the sequence/approach.

description.q: "If you are uncertain about a fact, state your uncertainty rather than presenting a guess as fact" is an example of:
description.explanation: Performance description sets behavioural expectations for how the AI should act.

description.q: According to the module, the more precisely you describe the product:
description.explanation: Precise product description reduces the iteration required.

options: Simply writing one good one-line prompt
Far more than a prompt — a structured approach to what you want, how to approach it, and how the AI should behave
Relevant only when using the API
description.explanation: Description is a structured approach, not just a single good prompt.

prompting.q: How many core prompting techniques does the curriculum identify?
prompting.explanation: Anthropic's curriculum identifies six core prompting techniques.

prompting.q: "Before drafting your recommendation, outline the key factors and any trade-offs" applies which technique?
prompting.explanation: Requesting reasoning before conclusions ('think first') improves accuracy.

prompting.q: Providing a sample email or report structure so the AI has a concrete target is which technique?
prompting.explanation: Showing examples gives the AI a concrete target rather than an abstract instruction.

prompting.q: Which is described as the powerful "meta-technique"?
options: Asking AI to help you write a better prompt
prompting.explanation: Asking AI to help you write an effective prompt is the meta-technique.

prompting.q: "You are a meticulous proofreader" vs "You are a creative brainstorming partner" illustrates which technique?
prompting.explanation: Setting a clear role shapes the AI's behaviour and output.

discernment.q: Why is confident, fluent-sounding AI output particularly dangerous?
options: Confidence in presentation does not correlate with accuracy of content
discernment.explanation: AI can sound authoritative while being wrong — presentation confidence does not equal accuracy.

options: Whether the AI maintained instructed behaviour
Whether the output itself is accurate, sound, and fit for purpose
discernment.explanation: Product discernment evaluates what the AI produced — accuracy, logic, real citations, fitness for purpose.

discernment.q: Checking whether the AI followed your specified steps and did not invent information describes:
discernment.explanation: Process discernment examines the AI's reasoning and whether it filled gaps with invented information.

discernment.q: When AI output is not right, the module says the usual answer is to:
options: Refine your description and try again
discernment.explanation: The fix is to refine your description and iterate — the feedback loop between discernment and description.

discernment.q: How is Discernment characterised relative to the other competencies?
options: The most critical skill — without it, even perfect delegation and description are dangerous
Only needed when using the API
discernment.explanation: Discernment is described as the most critical skill in AI fluency.

dd-loop.q: The Description-Discernment Loop is best described as:
options: A sign that you have failed
The iterative cycle of describe → evaluate → refine until the output meets your standards
dd-loop.explanation: It is the iterative engine of effective collaboration — and how skilled users normally work, not a failure.

options: Ask for a complete final draft immediately
Work in layers — outline first, review it, then expand section by section
Ask the AI to critique itself
dd-loop.explanation: The Building Pattern works in layers with control points at each stage.

dd-loop.q: "Review what you produced — what are the three weakest points and what assumptions should I verify?" is which pattern?
dd-loop.explanation: The Challenging Pattern asks the AI to critique its own work.

dd-loop.q: If three or four iterations are NOT converging on a good outcome, it may signal that:
options: You should accept the result as-is
The task may not be well-suited for AI, or your approach needs restructuring
You simply need a much longer prompt
dd-loop.explanation: Non-convergence can signal the task isn't suited for AI or needs a restructured approach.

dd-loop.q: South African professionals found the loop especially valuable for:
options: Tasks involving local context, where first output may use international conventions or miss jurisdiction-specific requirements
dd-loop.explanation: The refinement cycle is where you inject local expertise and jurisdiction-specific knowledge.

diligence.q: What is the fundamental principle of Deployment Diligence?
options: The AI is responsible for its own output
If your name goes on it, you are responsible for its contents — regardless of AI assistance
Verification is optional for low-risk tasks
Disclosure of AI use is never required
diligence.explanation: AI is a tool; the professional who uses it owns the result and its accuracy.

diligence.q: Under which South African law do businesses have specific obligations regarding processing personal information?
diligence.explanation: POPIA governs personal-information processing obligations for South African businesses.

diligence.q: Creation diligence is mainly concerned with:
options: What data you provide to AI, where it is processed/stored, and whether the provider trains on it
diligence.explanation: Creation diligence is about choosing and using AI responsibly, including data handling and provider training practices.

diligence.q: What is the module's stance on verifying AI-assisted output that will be shared or acted upon?
options: It is not optional — a qualified human must review it and own its accuracy
It is only needed for legal work
diligence.explanation: Verification is not optional; a qualified human must take ownership of accuracy and appropriateness.

options: When and how to disclose that AI assisted, with the global trend moving toward greater transparency
diligence.explanation: Transparency diligence concerns honest disclosure of AI's role; concealment erodes trust disproportionately.

claude-101.explanation: Claude is Anthropic's assistant designed to be helpful, harmless, and honest.

claude-101.q: What does Claude's large context window enable?
options: Processing entire documents, contracts, and reports in a single conversation
Avoiding the need to write prompts
claude-101.explanation: The context window lets Claude process whole documents at once rather than fragments.

claude-101.q: What is the Projects feature used for?
options: Creating workspaces with standing instructions that every conversation in them inherits
claude-101.explanation: Projects let you set standing instructions inherited by every conversation in that workspace.

claude-101.q: Which responsible-design trait of Claude does the module highlight?
options: It always gives a confident answer
It tends to flag uncertainty rather than fabricate answers
claude-101.explanation: Claude is designed to be conservative and flag uncertainty — valuable for professional work.

claude-101.q: What does the module say about Anthropic and data from paid plans?
options: Anthropic does not train on conversations from paid plans (Pro, Team, Enterprise)
claude-101.explanation: Anthropic does not train on paid-plan conversations — important for confidentiality and sensitive data.

api.q: Compared with the web interface, what does the Claude API give you control over?
options: System prompts, conversation management, output formatting, and integration with your systems
api.explanation: The API adds programmatic control over system prompts, conversation management, formatting, and integration.

options: Sending the response progressively (word by word) for a responsive experience
api.explanation: Streaming returns the response progressively, as most chat interfaces do.

api.q: Why is "Structured Output" from the API valuable?
options: It returns responses in specific formats (e.g., JSON) that an application can process programmatically
It removes the need for system prompts
api.explanation: Structured output (e.g., JSON) lets applications integrate AI output into automated workflows.

api.q: How do API system prompts differ from web-interface project instructions?
options: They can be generated dynamically based on the user, context, or task
They are always shown to end users
They are exactly the same thing
api.explanation: API system prompts can be dynamically generated per user/context/task, unlike static project instructions.

api.q: The module frames the move from individual AI fluency to organisational AI strategy as where what becomes valuable?
options: Switching to a different AI vendor
api.explanation: Building AI into products/processes needs strategic clarity — where Imbila's consulting and implementation support adds value.
